test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (AAO) 2023 Official Paper-III (Held On: 27 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In relation to the ledger, which of the following statements is INCORRECT?

options.text: The net result of all the transactions in respect of a particular account on a given date can be ascertained only from the ledger.
A ledger is the principal book of accounting system.
A ledger contains different accounts, wherein transactions relating to that account are recorded.
A ledger is the collection of all the accounts - whether debited or credited - in the journal proper, excluding various special journals.

solution:
The correct answer is **A ledger is the collection of all the accounts - whether debited or credited - in the journal proper, excluding various special journals.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **A ledger is the collection of all the accounts - whether debited or credited - in the journal proper, excluding various special journals:**

 
 
• This statement is incorrect because a ledger includes all accounts that have been debited or credited, including those from special journals like the sales journal, purchase journal, cash receipts journal, and cash payments journal. Special journals are used to record specific types of transactions, but their totals are ultimately posted to the ledger.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The net result of all the transactions in respect of a particular account on a given date can be ascertained only from the ledger:**

 
 
• This statement is correct. The ledger provides a consolidated view of all transactions affecting a particular account, allowing the net result to be determined on any given date.
 
 
 
• **A ledger is the principal book of accounting system:**
 
 
• This statement is correct. The ledger is often referred to as the principal or main book of accounts, as it contains all the financial transactions categorized by account.
 
 
 
• **A ledger contains different accounts, wherein transactions relating to that account are recorded:**
 
 
• This statement is correct. The ledger is organized into different accounts, each representing a specific type of transaction or financial element (e.g., assets, liabilities, equity, revenue, and expenses).
